media_strategy.selection_principle: LEAN media budget for this run: one generated hero image only; everything else is free data-driven visuals (Vega-Lite charts, an HTML/JS interactive, CSS stat callouts). No video, no audio, no generated music.

chart.reason: The dataset is fundamentally about counts over time and group differences — trend, ranking and group-diff charts carry the whole argument.

image.reason: A single atmospheric hero of Oxford architecture sets period and place before the data begins. Exactly one generated image per the run's strict LEAN budget.

video.reason: Run budget forbids video. The dataset is dates/founders/namesakes with no event or transformation that a clip would clarify better than a timeline chart.

audio.reason: Run budget forbids generated music/sonification. There is no sonic dimension to college founding dates that would explain anything beyond decoration.

interactive_or_map.reason: The 'oldest college' rivalry is a perfect guess-first reveal; no geographic dimension exists (all colleges are in one city) so a quiz, not a map, is the right interactive.

des_hero.label: Atmospheric Oxford hero image

content.prompt: Cinematic wide atmospheric photograph of ancient Oxford college spires and honey-colored stone quadrangles at golden hour, layered architectural depth from medieval Gothic towers to modern facades fading into mist, dramatic raking light, editorial fine-art photography, muted warm palette of amber and slate, no people, no text, no signage

des_hero.brief: Full-bleed hero behind the headline. Warm amber/slate Oxford skyline at golden hour, layered from medieval to modern. A dark gradient overlay at the bottom lets white headline text sit cleanly on top. No text baked into the image.
des_hero.rationale: One restrained, period-setting still grounds an abstract dates dataset in a real place before the charts begin. Image, not video, per the LEAN budget.

des_01.label: Guess the oldest college (quiz) + reveal chart

content.initial_state: Three face-down cards labelled University College, Balliol, Merton with the prompt 'Which is Oxford's oldest college?'
content.trigger: Reader clicks one card to commit a guess
content.transition: All three flip to show founding years 1249 / 1263 / 1264; a small horizontal year-line then fades in placing the trio (plus Rewley Abbey 1201 and St Edmund Hall 1278) on a timeline.
content.payoff: Reveal text: there is no single right answer — each claims 'oldest' on a different basis (endowment / continuous site / first statutes). The reader's pick is acknowledged but the point is the unresolvable 15-year cluster.

des_01.brief: A guess-first interaction. Reader picks one of three colleges, then all flip to reveal years and a compact timeline strip shows the six earliest foundations with Univ/Balliol/Merton highlighted and Rewley Abbey/Gloucester marked as defunct. Vanilla JS, no library; the timeline strip is a flex row of positioned dots with year labels, scaled across 1201-1283.
des_01.rationale: The finding is surprising and rivalry-driven — letting the reader commit before the reveal lands the 'unwinnable argument' far better than a static bar chart.

des_02.label: Foundations per century — two-wave column chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with century and exact count

style.palette: warm amber bars, 18th-century bar muted/grey to mark the trough, no gridlines, large axis labels

des_02.brief: Vertical bar chart, one bar per century (13th -> 21st, plus a faint 'unknown' bar). Bars in warm amber; the 18th-century bar (value 1) rendered in a desaturated grey to make the trough between the two waves pop. X axis ordered chronologically. Title-free; let the surrounding prose carry meaning.
des_02.rationale: A single decisive comparison across centuries — the double hump and the deep 18th-century valley read instantly in a column chart.

des_03.label: Largest gaps before a foundation — horizontal bars

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing the college, its founding year, and the gap in years

style.palette: amber bars, Keble (156) in deep accent color, sorted descending by gap, no gridlines

des_03.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the five longest gaps before a new foundation, sorted longest-first so Keble's 156-year gap sits on top in a strong accent color. Y axis = college (the one that ended the gap), X axis = gap_years. Each bar labelled with the founding year in the tooltip.
des_03.rationale: The Georgian silence is best shown as length — a horizontal bar literally pictures the 156-year wait as the longest bar.

des_04.label: Current vs defunct stat callout

content.label: Oxford colleges in this dataset no longer stand alone

des_04.brief: Large 64px stat '11 of 50' with the label below. Place above the status chart to set up the demolition framing.
des_04.rationale: The defunct count is the surprise that flips 'building boom' into 'demolition' — it deserves headline size.

des_05.label: Status split — current vs defunct/merged

content.interaction: hover tooltip with status and count

style.palette: current in amber, defunct/merged in slate-grey, no gridlines, large labels

des_05.brief: Two-bar chart: current (39) vs defunct/merged (11). Defunct bar in muted slate to read as 'lost'. Simple and decisive, paired beneath the stat callout.
des_05.rationale: A two-bar comparison is the most literal way to show how much of the list is gone; no exploration needed.

des_06.label: The modern boom — foundations by decade

content.interaction: hover tooltip with decade and count

style.palette: amber bars, the 1870s and 1960s bars (both value 5) in deep accent to mark the two micro-booms, no gridlines

des_06.brief: Column chart of foundations per decade from the 1870s to the 2010s. The two peak decades (1870s and 1960s, both 5) highlighted in a strong accent color to show the women's-college and graduate-college bursts; quieter decades in standard amber.
des_06.rationale: Decade granularity reveals the two clustered bursts that the century chart hides — exactly the engine of the modern wave.

des_07.label: Website as survival marker — grouped bars

content.interaction: hover tooltip with status, website-state, and count

style.palette: has_website in living amber, no_website in slate-grey, no gridlines

des_07.brief: Grouped/stacked bar: two groups (current, defunct/merged), each split into has_website vs no_website. Current = 39 amber / 0 grey; defunct = 1 amber / 10 grey. The near-total grey of the defunct group visually = the death certificate. Tooltip notes Templeton as the lone amber defunct bar that redirects to Green Templeton.
des_07.rationale: The grouped bar makes the near-perfect correlation between 'has a website' and 'still exists' immediately visible — the closing image of the piece.

page_rhythm.tone: warm editorial on near-white, archival/scholarly with a single atmospheric hero
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-first: prose states the finding, the chart or interactive lands directly below it
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Open with a guess-first card interaction rather than a chart; reserve the one generated image strictly for the hero; use a desaturated trough bar and a slate 'dead' palette so charts carry emotional weight without extra media. No audio card, no video — the restraint is the design.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Serif (Georgia) body within a 720px column; system-ui for chart labels and the quiz UI. Stat callout at 64px. Highlight color = deep amber/burnt-orange accent against muted slate for 'lost' items. Section dividers as thin rules.
